message.content:
Let  
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\0&-2\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathbf v=\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
A\mathbf v=\begin{pmatrix}2x+3y\\-2y\end{pmatrix},
\]
so
\[
\|A\mathbf v\|^2=(2x+3y)^2+(-2y)^2
=4x^2+12xy+13y^2.
\]
We need the maximum of this quadratic subject to \(\|\mathbf v\|^2=x^2+y^2=1\).

This is equivalent to finding the largest eigenvalue of
\[
A^TA=\begin{pmatrix}4&6\\6&13\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The eigenvalues satisfy
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}4-\lambda&6\\6&13-\lambda\end{pmatrix}
=(4-\lambda)(13-\lambda)-36
=\lambda^2-17\lambda+16=0.
\]
Thus
\[
(\lambda-1)(\lambda-16)=0,
\]
so the largest eigenvalue is \(16\). Therefore
\[
\max_{\|\mathbf v\|=1}\|A\mathbf v\|=\sqrt{16}=4.
\]
So the smallest possible constant is \(4\), and it is achieved, for example, by \(\mathbf v=(1,2)\).

The answer is \(\boxed{4}\).
